description.narrative: Improve the performance of Ukraine's social assistance and social services system for low-income households and provide income support to households affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic

The Social Security Nets Modernization Project of Ukraine bjective is to improve the performance of Ukraine?s social assistance and social services system for low-income families. All three components are linked through the definition of the Project?s Results Framework. Component one improving social assistance provision to the most vulnerable will support the Government?s reform agenda within three specific results areas, namely by: (i) accelerating poverty reduction through the gradual expansion of the GMI program; (ii) strengthening SSN administration to ensure efficient oversight and controls in both social assistance and social services delivery, and improved data management tools (MIS system) to support operational decisions and policy making; and (iii) aiding in the provision of effective social support to families in need and vulnerable families through integrating provision of benefits and services and supporting de-institutionalization of children?s services. Component two is supportive investments for institutional strengthening for administration of social assistance and social services. This component finances provision of goods, non-consulting services, consultants? services, training and operating costs to support strengthening the institutional capacities of the Ministry of Social Policy of Ukraine and local offices to implement and monitor benefits and service. Component three is supportive investments for increasing provision of family-based care to support orphans, children deprived of parental care, disabled children and vulnerable families in four oblasts. This component finances investments to support: i) childcare de-institutionalization by providing orphans and children deprived of parental care with a family environment through foster care, adoption and placement in family-type homes; ii) transformation of residential institutions; and iii) purchasing of new services from private and non-governmental providers for vulnerable families.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :LA: Covenant 1 - Institutional arrangement for Project Execution | Description :Project Operational Manual hasbeen elaborated by the MoSP, reviewed and no-objected by the World Bank team and approved by the order of the MoSP in September2014. The Administrative Agreement between the MoSP, MoF and USIF has been prepared and sent for World Bank team review. At the endof October, 2014 the Bank no-objected the Administrative Agreement. After project restructuring in February 2020 and excluding USIFfrom the list of project implementing agencies, this Administrative Agreement was canceled | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :LA: Covenant 2 - Investments in Social Facilities | Description :The MoSP has prepared and signed memorandum ofunderstanding with the following pilot oblasts, namely with city of Kyiv, Kyivslaya oblast, Odeska, Ternipilska, Pivnenska,Zakarpatska and Poltavska oblasts for supervision of the investment in internats and family homes in these selected oblasts; |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :LA: Covenant 3 - Environmental and Social Safeguards | Description :The Project Operational Manual includesprovisions regulating the environmental safeguards for civil works to be implemented by USIF. However after project restructuringin February 2019 the civil works under Component 3 were excluded from the project and, consequently the USIF was excluded from theagencies that could implement project. Operational Manual was updated to reflect these changes. Thus, there are no civil worksunder the project. | Due Date :01-May-2014

Finance Agreement :LA: Covenant 4 - Review by the Bank of Procurement Decisions | Description : Procurement Progress has beentracking by the MoSP in their semiannual monitoring reports. the World bank team regularly received these reports. We have provideda waiver for submission of the Procurement Progress Report that were suppose to cover October 2014- November 2015 period. InDecember 2017 and then in December 2018 the World Bank team received Procurement progress report that covered procurement progressand issues for 2015-2018 period of project implementation. The World Bank team reviewed the report and exchanged views on thisreport | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :LA: Covenant 5 - Withdrawal condition | Description :In 2 years the MoSP achieved 4 DLIs out of 17 DLIs anddisbursed US$70 million. All these withdrawals were made after the MoSP has submitted evidence satisfactory to the Bank thatpayments under the EEP have been made to eligible beneficiaries by the Borrower in accordance and in compliance with the proceduresset forth in the Borrower's applicable legislation. The World bank team checked the evidence submitted by the MoSP | Frequency:CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: The monthly number of GMI beneficiary families reached increased from 160 thousand in 2012 to 235 thousand in 2024

comment.narrative: The GoU gradually increased the eligibility income threshold for able-to-work family members from 21% of the Subsistence Minimum (SM) in 2015 to 55% in 2024 and 60% in 2025 and the income threshold for children - from 85% of the SM in 2015 to 140% in 2024 and 145% in 2025. In 2022, the average monthly number of GMI beneficiary families was 216,000. During 2023, it decreased to 173,000 due to the freeze of the SM, the outflow of Ukrainians to Europe, and the fact that around 20% of the Ukrainian territory is not under GoU control, where the application for benefits is not possible. Following the 2024 income threshold increases, this PDI reached 227,245, which is 7,755 short of the target value of 235,000.

title.narrative: An effective and efficient system to prevent, detect, deter and monitor error, fraud and corruption (EFC) in place

comment.narrative: In 2020, the GoU established its National Social Service of Ukraine (NSSU), a state executive body to perform oversight of the programs and to prevent fraud and error. Three inspections of the GMI program were made by way of random sampling, data matching, and risk-based profiling. In 2021, the NSSU inspected its housing and utilities subsidy (HUS) program using the data matching technology, which revealed that the technology used had a high detection rating, thus confirming that the system operates effectively.

title.narrative: Share of women-entrepreneurs among able to work GMI beneficiaries who benefited from the start-up grants for small business development increases

comment.narrative: Provision of financial support to self-employment and small business development for GMI beneficiaries was planned to be launched in January 2022. On February 24, 2022, the provision of financial start-up grants has been put on hold during the martial law. However, in March 2023 the GoU allocated funds in the State Budget to provide financial support to small business development for GMI beneficiaries. In 2023 only women were provided with start-up grants. 10 women were given financial assistance to start a business in 2023, thus the share of women among beneficiaries of start-up grants is 100%.

title.narrative: Share of women among able to work GMI beneficiaries benefitting from the activation services increases

comment.narrative: Activation services for GMI beneficiaries were launched in January 2021. The baseline was established at the end of 2021 at 68.6 percent. The baseline was determined using number of women among able to work GMI beneficiaries who were registered with the employment service bodies during 2021. The data are provided by the Information and Processing Data Center of the MoSP and showed that in 2022 share of women among able to work GMI beneficiaries benefitting from the activation services increased to 76.7%. Comparison of the annual 2021 and 2022 data shows the increase by 8.1%. In 2023 this share of women increased to 79.7% and in 2024 - to 80.6%. Thus, the cumulative increase is 12%.

title.narrative: Number of amalgamated communities that have implemented participatory budgeting increases

comment.narrative: Data on participatory budgeting implemented by territorial communities (TC) were collected by March 1 of each year. Number of amalgamated communities that have implemented participatory budgeting increased from 24 TC in 2018 to 197 in 2021. The target was achieved, and no further monitoring was possible due to the February 24, 2022, crisis in Ukraine.
